title: A method for the permeabilization of live Drosophila melanogaster larvae to small molecules and cryoprotectants
author: Alex Murray
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.75xhq7n
materials: Keywords: Drosophila, larvae, permeabilization, imaging, cryopreservation, method.
Larvae can be permeabilized to fluorescein diacetate
Larvae were permeabilized to ethylene glycol and DMSO
Development of the Permeabilization solution and protocol

WT larvae of various stages were collected and placed into a glass dissecting plate. Larvae were then exposed to 10-50% heptane diluted in D-limonene (both Sigma) for time periods between 100 and 45 seconds. After treatment, larvae were soaked in 62.5 µg/ml fluorescein diacetate (FDA) in DPBS. Fluorescein diacetate uptake was imaged using florescent microscopy at 488nm with a Leica MZ10F microscope and Leica Las X software. Surviving larvae were transferred to fresh media and monitored for development to adulthood.

WT larvae were permeabilized using the optimised method above. They were then exposed to CPA solution (25% EG, 25% DMSO in DPBS) (all Sigma) for 20 minutes. Larvae were observed to determine survival, defined as continued wriggling.

steps.title: Collect third‑instar larvae
steps.instruction: Using a handling needle or tweezers, pick healthy third‑instar Drosophila melanogaster larvae and transfer them onto a glass dissecting dish (plastic may be damaged by limonene).

steps.title: Apply permeabilization solution
steps.instruction: Cover the larvae with ~300 µL of permeabilization solution consisting of 10 % (v/v) heptane and 90 % (v/v) D‑limonene and expose them for exactly 45 seconds; longer times increase mortality. Remove the solution as quickly as possible after the exposure.

steps.title: Remove excess solvent
steps.instruction: Aspirate and discard the permeabilization solution, then immediately blot the larvae dry with tissue paper to eliminate residual heptane/limonene.

steps.title: Add test substance
steps.instruction: Immediately cover the blotted larvae with the substance you wish to deliver (e.g., fluorescein diacetate or a cryoprotectant solution). Exposure time must be optimised for each specific compound.

steps.title: Incubate with fluorescein diacetate (FDA)
steps.instruction: Soak the permeabilized larvae in fluorescein diacetate solution for 20 minutes, then image the larvae by fluorescence microscopy (excitation ≈488 nm) to assess dye uptake.

steps.title: Incubate with cryoprotectant solution
steps.instruction: After permeabilization, soak the larvae in a cryoprotectant (CPA) solution containing 25 % ethylene glycol and 25 % DMSO in DPBS (v/v) for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Assess survival and development
steps.instruction: Monitor immediate survival by checking for wriggling after 20 minutes; continue to rear larvae to adulthood and record the proportion that reach adulthood and reproduce.
